2. The record shows that despite service, respondent nos. 5 to 9 have chosen not to appear before this Court.

sentences.text: By this Writ Petition, the petitioner is seeking a direction for disbursal of compensation amount under the Award with respect to acquisition of property at CTS No. 670 admeasuring 178.2 sq. feet situated at Village-Amboli, Taluka-Andheri, Mumbai Suburban District.
The petitioner is claiming 4/5 share in the compensation which was payable to respondent nos. 5 to 8.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, respondent nos. 5 to 8 sold their respective shares in the said property as per registered sale deeds executed in the year 2006, much prior to the Notification of acquisition issued on 04.03.2009 under the provisions of Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act,
1974 ("the Act", for short).

entities.text:
Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority Act,
1974
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Copies of the sale deeds have been placed on record, and on the basis of such documents, it is asserted that the petitioner is entitled for disbursal of 4/5 share of the compensation that would have been payable to the vendors i.e. respondent nos. 5 to 8.
4.
It is submitted that such a dispute under the provisions of the said Act could have been referred to a Tribunal constituted under Section 41 thereof.
The petitioner was constrained to file the writ petition, as no such Tribunal existed at the time when the writ petition was filed.

In support thereof,
a response to a query put under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is relied upon, which states that as on 16.09.2019, the Tribunal under Section 41 of the said Act, was not constituted.
02 December 2025 Rajeshri Aher 903 WP 3133 OF 2019(OS).DOC 5. The learned Addl. G.P. informs this Court that even today such a Tribunal is not in existence.
Hence, we are satisfied that the petitioner is entitled to maintain the present writ petition for the limited relief sought towards disbursal of 4/5 share of the compensation amount.

6. The learned Addl. G.P. submitted that when such a prayer was made before the respondent no.4,
it was made clear that it could not be granted, as the Award was already pronounced, and thereupon the respondent no.4 had been rendered functus officio.

7. The learned counsel appearing for Respondent No.3- M.M.R.D.A. submitted that in the light of the aforesaid registered sale deeds executed in favour of the petitioner, respondent no.3 had approached respondent no.4 for disbursal of the share belonging to respondent nos. 5 to 8 to the petitioner, but, no action was taken on the said request other than stating that respondent no. 4 had been rendered functus officio.
8.
We have perused the documents on record.

By a registered sale deed dated 13.09.2006,
respondent no.5 sold his share to the petitioner.

Similarly, by a registered sale deed dated 06.10.2006, respondent no.7 sold her share to the petitioner and by a registered sale deed dated 20.10.2006, respondent nos. 6 and 8 sold their respective shares to the petitioner.

These sale deeds concerned the subject property, which was then acquired by respondent nos. 1 to 4.
9.

sentences.text: 2 share of respondent no. 9 was disbursed to him.
In that light, we find that none of the respondent nos. 5 to 9 can raise an objection to the prayer made in the present petition.

10. Even if the stand taken by respondent no. 4 of being rendered functus officio is to be accepted,
there can be no impediment for this Court to exercise writ jurisdiction in the interest of justice to grant the prayer made by the petitioner in this petition.

11. In view of the above, the writ petition is allowed in terms of prayer Clause (a), which reads as follows:
"(a) This Hon'ble Court be pleased to issue a writ of mandamus or a writ in the nature of mandamus ordering, directing & mandating the Respondent Nos. 1 to 4 to disburse 4/5 share of the compensation/amount under award with respect to the subject property bearing CTS No. 670, admeasuring about 178.2 sq. ft. situated at Village-Amboli, Taluka-Andheri, Mumbai Suburban District acquired under the provision of said Act in accordance with law and/or under Government Resolution or policies framed by the State Government for higher and better compensation to owners of the lands;"
12.
Accordingly further steps shall be taken by respondent no.4 for correcting the record and calling upon the petitioner to produce necessary documents for disbursal of the 4/5 share of compensation.
The said amount shall be disbursed alongwith accrued interest in accordance with law.
The exercise shall be 02 December 2025 Rajeshri Aher 903 WP 3133 OF 2019(OS).DOC carried out within a period of eight weeks from today.
Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
(MANJUSHA DESHPANDE, J.) (MANISH PITALE, J.) { 02 December 2025 Rajeshri Aher Gehlot M. Shafi vs The State Of Maharashtra And 8 Ors.
